title: Frobenius-periodic vector bundles glue along the almost blowup square of an equation in two generators, giving an equivalence of categories
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter flat.tex (More on Flatness), section 'The local structure of a finite type module'
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file flat.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: In characteristic p, for the almost blowup square X, X', Z, E attached to two equations f_1, f_2, the lemma asserts that the functor G from the F-periodic vector bundles on X to the compatible pairs of F-periodic bundles on Z and X' is an equivalence (statement lines 12302-12316). Both directions need a genuine descent argument at the level of the colimit: full faithfulness requires choosing N large enough that maps on Z and X' agree over E, passing to a finite affine cover on which the bundles are free, replacing the colimit of global sections by the fibre product of the three colimits in the almost blowup square, and then gluing the resulting local maps after a further increase of N (proof lines 12319-12353). Essential surjectivity reduces first to the Noetherian case by descending the triple along a finitely generated subalgebra, then to X Noetherian and F = O_Z^{oplus r}, where the author uses that the ideal of E is globally generated by f_1 and f_2, that a globally generated quasi-coherent module on E = P^1_Z has vanishing H^1, and the theorem on formal functions to lift a compatible trivialisation of G along E to a map O_{X'}^{oplus r} -> G that is an isomorphism in a neighbourhood of E, and finally two Zariski glueing arguments (proof lines 12356-12437). The interaction of the Frobenius colimit with the three charts of the almost blowup square is the non-formal content, so the claim is H2.
